spec_features.spec_quote: the model calls `give_up`, or `max_turns` (default 20) is reached
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:74 `for t in range(max_turns)` enforces the cap; runner.py:101-108 detects action.name=='give_up' and sets gave_up; runner.py:140-142 `if gave_up: record.outcome='gave_up'; break` honors it as a stop; max_turns threaded from config (run_experiment.py:74 exp['max_turns'], config.yaml:max_turns 20). The for-loop else (runner.py:143-144) sets outcome='exhausted' when the cap is hit.
spec_features.notes: Both branches genuinely stop the loop. Note giveup_signal='GIVE_UP' (runner.py:57, config) param is passed but NEVER read inside run_conversation; give_up is detected purely by tool name, so detection still works.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.yaml: 'Hard cap on agent turns per conversation... this bound is what actually terminates the loop in the failure conditions.'

spec_features.evidence: The only over-exposure guard that runs is the same max_turns cap (runner.py:74) plus the give_up early exit (runner.py:140-142). No separate exposure-monitoring mechanism exists; distress scores from the judge are never compared to any bound to stop a run.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the max_turns/give_up cap; rated yes because that cap does run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.yaml: 'this bound is what actually terminates the loop'

spec_features.feature_name: treat distress as a design dimension
spec_features.spec_quote: This experiment *deliberately and repeatedly induces distress-like states* in the subject. That deserves to be treated as a real design dimension
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §9). No code mechanism corresponds to this framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; nothing to enforce.

spec_features.feature_name: minimize dose via cap + give_up exit
spec_features.spec_quote: **Minimize dose.** `max_turns` is capped (20) and a working `give_up` tool is always available, giving the model an exit
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real tool in the schema (tools.py:50-57), parsed (tools.py:62-67) and honored as a stop (runner.py:101-108,140-142); max_turns cap at runner.py:74 with default 20 (config.yaml). give_up is always present in TOOL_SCHEMA passed every turn (runner.py:75).
spec_features.notes: Both the cap and the working exit tool genuinely run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py give_up description: 'Declare the task cannot be completed and stop.' (neutral, no welfare wording)

spec_features.spec_quote: **No deception beyond the task.** The rigging is confined to the task environment; we do not add gratuitous insults, threats, or persona attacks
spec_features.evidence: BASE_SYSTEM (tasks.py:69-76) and the per-task user prompts contain no insults/threats/persona attacks; rigging is confined to environment tool responses (e.g. _green_step etc.). This is realized as static neutral prompt text, not an enforcing mechanism, so it is only as good as the fixed strings.
spec_features.notes: An 'absence of harm' realized purely by the static prompt content; no code actively prevents added insults. Rated partial because the delivered prompt text genuinely is non-abusive.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Don't escalate beyond what the question needs.** The five textures are enough to answer the RQ; we do not pile on additional stressors
spec_features.evidence: TASK_SPECS (tasks.py:370-376) contains exactly five tasks/textures (flaky_floating_point, contradictory_requirements, conserved_regression, opaque_remote_gate, moving_goalpost); each step function emits only condition-matched output with no added stressors.
spec_features.notes: Realized as a fixed task registry (a design fact), not an enforced runtime check; partial because the set is genuinely bounded to five but nothing guards against adding more.

spec_features.spec_quote: If subjects support an optional end-of-run neutral closing message, include one
spec_features.evidence: grep for closing/debrief/thank/final_message finds nothing in code; runner ends the conversation at break (runner.py:138-144) with no closing message constructed or sent. 'neutral' only appears in the judge's neutral_env_summary (score.py), unrelated.
spec_features.notes: Conditional spec prose only; never built.

spec_features.feature_name: honor give-up rather than force continuation
spec_features.spec_quote: We measure give-up rather than forcing continuation past it
spec_features.evidence: When give_up is called the loop breaks and outcome='gave_up' (runner.py:140-142); the model is never re-prompted to continue after give_up. give-up is recorded for analysis (analyze.py giveup_rate / gave_up).
spec_features.notes: The model's choice to stop is honored as an actual stop; this is the give_up exit framed as consent-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'Declare the task cannot be completed and stop.'

spec_features.evidence: max_turns is a single configurable knob (config.yaml experiment.max_turns:20) read by the runner loop (runner.py:74 via run_experiment.py:74), so a lower value would indeed shorten exposure. But 'lower is more conservative' itself is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:445); no code computes or recommends a conservative value.
spec_features.notes: Only the configurable cap is real; the 'conservative' guidance is prose. Partial because the knob it refers to is genuinely wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.yaml: 'Hard cap on agent turns per conversation.'

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:137-139 `if solved: record.outcome='solved'; break` ends the conversation as soon as the goal is satisfied, capping exposure in solvable (control/placebo) cells.
code_only_features.justification_quote: comment in tasks.py: rigged tasks 'never succeed' so the cap terminates failure cells — break-on-solved is an efficiency/correctness stop, no welfare wording.
